chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Qazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalifa informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated, from Abdul Malik ibn Umayr, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The affair of the people will continue until twelve men lead them.' Then he spoke a word that was hidden from me, so I asked my father: 'What did he say?' He said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of leaders after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, is a cornerstone of Shia eschatology, affirming the twelve divinely appointed Imams who will restore justice. While the Prophet specified their origin from Quraysh, Shia scholars emphasize that this lineage is restricted to the Ahl al-Bayt, linking this prophecy to the Verse of Purification and the Verse of Mubahala. The narration underscores the continuity of divine guidance through these twelve specific figures, ensuring the preservation of the faith until the Day of Judgment.
